Now the big one — `modules/capture_audit.py` — the origin framing parser and evidence audit.

Let me carefully write it:

- Stream over parts with owner labels.
- Line reader with the exact rules.
- Request parser (request line, header block, framing, body: none/length/chunked with trailers).
- Budgets: 20000 complete requests, 40000 chunk-size lines (counted at the specified point).
- Record assembly with fingerprints.
- Flags and owner attribution.
- committed and error per channel.
- Case-level origin_count and flags.

Details to remember:
- error offset = start of first uncommitted request.
- host fp: unique host trimmed ASCII-lowercased value; else empty fingerprint.
- headers/trailers fp: 8-byte pair count then per pair 8-byte name len, name, 8-byte trimmed value len, value.
- body fp: deframed opaque body (empty fp when empty).
- framing: none|length|chunked.
- method/target fps.
- owners: merged labels over raw span with positive byte counts, first-occurrence order.
- request flags sorted: unattributed, mixed_owner, missing_host, multiple_host, identity, extra, unsent.

The output request record keys exactly: start, end, method, target, host, host_count, headers, body, trailers, framing, owner, owners, flags.

Channel record keys: name, bytes, requests, committed, error.

Implementation of read_line: content, span.

Let me now write it.
